content:
The Australian government has appointed former Liberal minister Philip Ruddock to lead a review examining the adequacy of Australian law in protecting religious freedom. The announcement, made on Wednesday, aims to address a contentious debate concerning religious amendments within a same-sex marriage bill. Treasurer Scott Morrison has stated that the review will not replace these amendments.

***

Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull emphasized the importance of carefully examining religious freedom in the context of the recent "yes" vote for same-sex marriage and the upcoming legislation. This review precedes proposed legislation surrounding same-sex marriage, as it is suggested by senior conservatives the matter be handled in the new year. Other conservatives want it to be considered at the same time.

***

Ruddock's task involves producing a report by March 31st, assessing the existing legal framework for religious freedom. A variety of alterations to amend the laws regarding religious freedom have been proposed, with the government hesitant to implement changes that extend beyond the specific context of marriage equality to avoid potential legal issues.

***

Turnbull highlighted the potential for unintended consequences when legislating protections for fundamental rights like freedom of religion, especially through broad declarations. The government is apprehensive about unspecified legislation similar to bill of rights’ style declarations.

***

The prime minister lauded Ruddock's appointment, citing his experience as Australia's special envoy for human rights as a key qualification for the role. The review is intended to provide expert insight into potentially useful legislative reforms.
